native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: Individuals with a criminal record (ever_jailed=1) had significantly lower wealth than those without in all three years measured (1985, 1990, 1996): mean wealth shortfall of ~$17k in 1985, ~$58k in 1990, and ~$85k in 1996 (medians 720 vs 3,600; 0 vs 10,500; 0 vs 8,500), significant in raw tests (Welch t, Mann-Whitney, median test; all Holm-adjusted p<1e-8), after adjusting for race and sex (HC1-robust OLS, p<=2.6e-07), and — for 1990 and 1996 — after additionally controlling 1985 baseline wealth (p<=1.2e-06). Because jail status spans 1985-1994, the significant 1985 gap indicates pre-incarceration selection, while the larger, baseline-adjusted gaps in 1990/1996 are consistent with an additional incarceration-associated wealth penalty.
native_result.WorkflowB: Inspected dataset (12,013 rows, no missingness; wealth composites right-skewed with zeros/negatives/extreme tails). Per year: Welch t-test, Mann-Whitney U, median test, bootstrap 95% CI of mean difference (5,000 resamples), Cliff's delta. Covariate-adjusted OLS with HC1 robust SEs (ever_jailed + race + sex); for 1990/1996 also controlled 1985 baseline wealth. Signed-log wealth sensitivity regressions. Holm correction across the three years for each test family. All conclusions robust across tests, adjustment sets, and correction.
